ms.report:
Overview
The open source setup for the new Voices project has been completed according to specifications of Milestone 1 - including testing, documentation, licensing, and guidance for community feedback / contributions.
Additionally, a minimally functional voting module has been deployed to the Catalyst Testnet.
Finally, a continuous testing strategy that leverages voting events on the Catalyst Testnet has been published to Gitbook. 
Presentation
These deliverables were presented to an After Town Hall audience 6/December. During that recorded session, each of these deliverables were reviewed in depth, with an emphasis on covering each of the milestone outputs described in the statement of milestones. 
Reviewers are invited to watch that recorded session here. The slides covered during the presentation can be found here. Note that the recording and slide deck cover two proposals - Hermes and Voices. The Voices specific content can be found starting at 16:30 in the recording, and Slide 6 in the slides.

Thank you for taking the time to review our milestone submission! We're excited to share our progress with you, and invite you to review our accomplishments from the past several months. We hope you enjoy reviewing this content as much as we enjoyed putting it together for you!
Summary
A new Cardano chain follower was developed to satisfy the backend enhancements for Milestone3. A recorded overview can be found here, and the code reviewed here. 
The chain follower allows the system to quickly index and query information from the Cardano network. It unlocks use cases that were previously impossible using existing solutions like db-sync, and offers approximately 100x sync time performance improvement compared to db-sync. 
The follower is capable of capturing legacy CIP36 registrations, as well as the new RBAC registrations, including rewards and payment information for each registration. The follower is flexible enough to target different snapshot dates based on parameters, query wallet details to check against role requirements, and allow the deadline for different roles to occur at different times. 
Additional backend enhancements were developed to store and query information collected by the chain follower. These include databases and endpoints for staked ADA / Cardano native tokens (demo & code), CIP36 registrations (demo & code), and RBAC registrations (demo & code). Endpoints also provide user data about registration history and errors. The CIP36 registrations demo also includes a demo of the permissionless authorization framework, which can be read more about here. 
A key enabler for the permissionless authorization implemented with the CIP36 registrations endpoint is the C509 certificate generation (demo & code). The initial implementation includes the ability to generate, verify, and decode certificates. Thank you for taking the time to review our milestone submission! We're excited to share our progress with you, and invite you to review our accomplishments from the past several months. We hope you enjoy reviewing this content as much as we enjoyed putting it together for you!

Account Creation & Proposal Submission UX (Web Browser UI)
The first frontend module for the new application has been developed, and is being prepared for use in the upcoming Fund14.
A high level introduction of the new app can be found here.
A more detailed walkthrough of the account creation and onboarding process can be viewed here. 
Key features include CIP30 wallet connect and role registrations for contributors and proposers submitted to Cardano mainnet (as outlined in the RBAC spec from previous milestones). 
As specified in the milestone, a valid role registration is required to access functionality like proposal submission. 
A demo of the primary Ideascale replacement functionality can be viewed here. 
Key features include Campaign & Category Details, Proposal Explorer, Proposal Editing & Publishing, and Comments. 
As specified in the milestone, the frontend reads the proposal format (including data validations) from the backend and formats it for data entry in the frontend. Proposals may be submitted as Draft or Final, with clear differentiation between them when being viewed by other users. 
As specified in the milestone, we will pilot the new proposal submission experience with at least 25 proposers to collect and incorporate community feedback. The new proposal submission capabilities will be piloted with the entire Catalyst community in Fund14, providing opportunity for hundreds of proposers to test new features and provide feedback. Over the course of Fund14, we will gather direct feedback from 25 proposers via user interview, as well as setting up a community wide feedback loop using a feedback form similar to the existing voting app exit survey.
